newsitem.title: FINLAND: Lively Helsinki ends off as Nokia loses momentum.
newsitem.headline: Lively Helsinki ends off as Nokia loses momentum.

text.p: Finnish shares end flat to a shade lower as Nokia comes off its highs set in an initial reaction to Swedish Ericsson's in-line Q4 report, brokers said.

Forestries trimmed recent gains, and the market was wary most day as European bourses were weighed down by a weak overnight close on Wall Street and a bout of jitters over political uncertainty in France.

The Helsinki HEX index closed 0.23 percent off at 2,877.79 after trading in the black most session, but the market was flat overall with as many advancers as decliners. The FOX derivatives and portfolio bechmark closed 0.53 percent down at 1,003.20.
Compared to last Friday, the HEX closed 1.9 percent higher.
Telecoms major Nokia closed at 306.50, up 0.50 markka but clearly off its 312.00 high, accounting for 30 percent of trade.

The forestry sub-index closed down 1.56 percent as industry leader UPM-Kymmene retreated 2.50 markka to 117.50. Second largest Enso closed flat at 43.50 markka, mostly unfazed by talk that it may buy German newsprint and magazine paper group E.Holtzmann.
Analysts said buying the group would be strategically good, but that some reported price demands seemed too high.
Next week's focus would be on Nokia's first quarter earnings due on Tuesday, and trade was seen quiet ahead of that.
The median of forecasts for Nokia's first quarter pretax profit was 1.26 billion markka, compared to 399 million markka reported in January-March 1996.
"Monday's are usually quiet and now with Nokia's results due on Tuesday -- there will be hardly any trade on Monday," said one broker.
Next week will be shorter, with markets closed for May Day holiday on Thursday, which could dent trading on Friday, brokers said.
